comment: The section distinguishes direct integration from interoperability and associates interoperability with open, publicly governed specifications. This is useful, but direct point-to-point exchanges can still be interoperable when both systems conform to the same reusable public specifications.

public.text: The section distinguishes direct integration from interoperability and associates interoperability with open, publicly governed specifications. This is useful, but direct point-to-point exchanges can still be interoperable when both systems conform to the same reusable public specifications.
public.suggestedRevision: Clarify that topology does not determine interoperability. A direct connection can be interoperable if it uses shared, reusable, publicly governed specifications and avoids bespoke bilateral semantics or behaviour.
